scope: Combined retained sample from the original top fifty and the completed ranks 51–100 expansion.

rule.month_high_restriction: restricted_body / post_records > 0.50, evaluated exactly as 2*restricted_body > post_records
rule.exclude_publication: high_restriction_months / observed_months >= 0.20, evaluated exactly as 5*high_restriction_months >= observed_months
rule.denominator: Calendar months within the study window containing at least one saved post record for that publication. Empty months are undefined shares and are not counted as unrestricted months.
rule.partial_first_last_months: Included if containing a post; excluding partial boundary months yields the same retained set.
rule.restriction_definition: Saved audience-restricted body status; public posts with no returned prose are a separate category, not recoded as restricted.
rule.filter_unit: Whole publication. Retain all its recorded months/posts/comments; do not drop only its restricted months.

decisions.alignment_rationale: The source explicitly describes political heterogeneity. Four sampled public texts are mostly technology and previews; they do not justify coding every contributor as right-wing or centrist.

A home for the politically homeless, organized around liberal democracy. Sample includes a Progressive editor and multiple distinct reporters; publication-level anti-Trump orientation does not identify each writer’s ideology.
The sampled account favors abortion rights and contrasts Democratic electoral gains with Republican extremism. The label is provisional, not inferred from anti-Trump criticism alone.
Resistance rhetoric and identification with Harris supporters accompany reporting. A named editorial network, not a single writer.

decisions.ideology: Left / progressive; editorial tendency across contributors
decisions.alignment_rationale: The larger public-text review includes affirmative economic-progressive advocacy for worker organizing and rejection of corporate influence, defenses of public healthcare coverage, and immigration analysis critical of restrictionism. This supports a broad progressive editorial tendency rather than merely an anti-Trump label. Zeteo publishes multiple authors and explicitly disclaims that each opinion is the organization’s own; do not assign every contributor the same ideology.
Contributors explicitly need not agree on issues. Profits support litigation against Trump; this distinguishes the hybrid organization from a generic newsroom.

Silver directly calls himself a moderate liberal and favors individual rights, free speech, decentralized decision-making and markets. A later essay explicitly places this form of liberalism closer to the center than the left. For a coarse three-way description, center/moderate liberal is the best working category. This does not mean neutral reporting, an exact ideological midpoint, or absence of liberal issue positions. Coding Silver as center-left is a reasonable sensitivity rather than calling him progressive-left or Republican.
Favors an immigration path to citizenship; sampled tariff and aid criticism supplies additional policy context. Do not infer a formal party identity.
Author explicitly identifies the product as satirical news. Satirical targets suggest orientation, but fictional statements cannot be treated as factual endorsements.
Favorable Harris comparison and inequality/corporate-power framing support a progressive, Democratic-aligned interpretation. The newsletter also includes a collaborator and interviews.

decisions.ideology: Center-left / liberal; civil-rights and labor emphasis
decisions.alignment_rationale: The reviewed Labor Day essay rejects Reagan’s small-government economic program, affirms organized labor and civil-rights work, and urges electoral action. The poll-tax essay defends expansive voting access and objects to exclusionary requirements. This is substantive liberal framing, not simply a biography as an Obama appointee. A detailed economic platform remains unmeasured.

Criticizes legacy-media accounts while also discussing Trump’s excesses. Free-speech positions and anti-establishment reporting do not by themselves establish Republican loyalty or a fixed left-right location.

Kinzinger explicitly identifies as center-right in his February 2024 essay and as a conservative and Republican in his August 2024 convention speech. His support for Harris is presented as a coalition choice despite policy differences. This resolves his within-window ideological location; it is not an assertion that every position or later post is conservative.

alignment_evidence.title: Why We Fight. The War Against Brain Worms

decisions.alignment_rationale: The separately reviewed pilot explicitly recommends incremental public health coverage, supply reform and Democratic coalition priorities. Supporting AOC for a committee role does not make the author a socialist.
Climate action, racial justice and democratic norms are positively valued. Team-authored pieces and staff changes require distinguishing Dan Rather from the Steady brand.

decisions.ideology: Center-left / socially liberal civic analysis; provisional
decisions.alignment_rationale: McMahon’s own public prose rejects firearm-worship arguments and asks that children not have access to guns, advocates a constitutional amendment limiting money in politics, and criticizes religious-political curriculum mandates. Together these support a tentative liberal-leaning/center-left editorial assessment. Independence and a calm tone are not the basis for this label. Fiscal policy and many other domains remain unmeasured. An independent gubernatorial guest’s self-description is not McMahon’s.
Judd Legum expressly identifies as progressive while stating that readers need not share his views. Former campaign employment is biographical evidence, not proof of present party obedience.

decisions.publication: Hope for America with Heather Delaney Reese
decisions.ideology: Center-left / liberal; social-protection and immigrant-rights emphasis
decisions.alignment_rationale: The Social Security essay affirmatively defends social insurance and Medicaid against cuts paired with tax benefits for the wealthy. Immigration commentary rejects scapegoating and calls for taking Congress back. These give positive social-protection and rights positions beyond generalized anti-MAGA criticism.

decisions.ideology: Left / progressive, with mixed contributor backgrounds
decisions.alignment_rationale: Self-description is progressive independent media, featuring Lincoln Project talent. Do not give every former Republican contributor the publication’s progressive label.

decisions.ideology: Center-left / moderate liberal; former Republican, Democratic-aligned
decisions.alignment_rationale: Schmidt’s 2024 autobiographical post says he left the GOP in 2018 and registered as a Democrat in 2020; it does not verify his registration today. More substantively, his own writing opposes reproductive restrictions and discrimination against gay people, and condemns the transfer of resources from working families and healthcare to wealthy interests. A moderate-liberal/center-left working label fits this current editorial material better than either Republican-conservative or merely unknown. A detailed economic ideology is not established.
Democratic gains are presented favorably alongside criticism of MAGA institutional control. This provides coalition evidence more clearly than a comprehensive policy ideology.
Explicitly presents anti-LGBTQ bills failing as victories. A strong issue position does not establish loyalty to every Democratic politician or an economic ideology.

Criticism of gender-policy progressivism and Biden coexists with extensive criticism of Trump’s executive power and election conduct. About page institutionalizes an edited dissent section; email selection is not the same as open comments.
The separately reviewed pilot explicitly defends intentionally positive Biden coverage and identifies itself as commentary rather than journalism. Electoral mobilization is also explicit.
Former Obama adviser explicitly offers a newsletter for defeating Trump and MAGA. Party strategy is better identified than the precise degree of economic progressivism.
Explicitly seeks a progressive future and defeating Trump; a later sampled rant criticizes Democrats’ weak opposition. Party commitment does not mean absence of intra-party criticism.
About page explicitly describes a largely progressive audience and a cast of contributors. Article-level legal analysis should not be conflated with a formal party institution.

decisions.ideology: Center-left / liberal; reproductive-rights and equal-protection emphasis
decisions.alignment_rationale: Two longer public pieces explicitly favor reproductive autonomy and defend abortion access while criticizing restrictions and attacks on healthcare provision. This supplies substantive liberal editorial evidence missing from the initial short-video sample. Multiple authors and advocacy partners contribute; do not attribute every piece to Michael Popok. Medical or legal factual claims are not adjudicated by this ideology review.
About page praises the Democratic Party and Biden; articles solicit money and volunteering for Democratic candidates. Degree of left economic ideology remains less certain than party commitment.

decisions.ideology: Center-left / socially liberal editorial framing; nonpartisan news brand
decisions.alignment_rationale: The editor’s own introductions affirm reproductive-rights work and characterize abortion restrictions and their consequences critically. The outlet also gives space to pragmatic Democratic figures and maintains a fact-explanation mission. This supports a tentative center-left editorial tendency without equating a nonpartisan news brand with centrism or assigning it a party identity. Guest views and poll findings are not coded as the editor’s own.
Explicitly works to elect Democratic candidates and supplies daily political actions. This is an organizing product rather than a general news agency.
A named Raw Story/Really American network describes itself as a people-powered response to MAGA media ownership. Multiple staff and brand bylines make individual attribution difficult.

decisions.publication: The Good in Us by Mary L. Trump
decisions.alignment_rationale: Urges Democratic leadership not to concede to Republicans. Many sampled records have missing bylines, so Mary Trump’s author identity cannot be assumed for all texts.

Wilson describes himself as neither progressive nor liberal and invokes moderate conservatism in his November 2023 Biden endorsement. His January 2024 essay explicitly identifies him as a conservative believer in free markets. This is current in-window self-description and affirmative economic orientation, rather than a label inferred solely from his former Republican career. Democratic electoral support is coded separately.

decisions.ideology: Center-left / pluralist liberal; cohosts have cross-cutting positions
decisions.alignment_rationale: Beth Silvers explicitly rejects identifying her conversational moderation with centrist policy views, describes welcoming immigration and left/libertarian criminal-justice positions, and calls a Democratic midterm victory imperative. Sarah identifies herself as a Democrat in a separate transcript. This resolves the broad outlet tendency while preserving differences between the cohosts; a shared tone is not a shared point on every issue.
About page explicitly calls the creator left; sampled essay advocates supporting even conservative Democrats over Republicans to secure governing power.

In an interview republished on his own newsletter, Sykes says his conservative principles have not changed and specifically retains disagreements over tax policy and student debt while endorsing Harris on democratic grounds. His own commentary situates this within a conservative anti-Trump coalition, with later criticism of MAGA and attention to Democratic moderation. This is a clearer current center-right/conservative case than the initial sampled excerpts showed. It is not pro-Trump.
Explicit progressive politics mission and talk-show identity; policy commentary plus songs, book excerpts and collaborators require genre separation.

decisions.publication: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
decisions.alignment_rationale: Explicitly attacks conservative politics, not just Trump personally. Insults and humorous labels are rhetorical style, not a numerical extremity scale.
Explicitly funds progressive voices and ideas. The Pod Save America brand includes many distinct authors and formats.

decisions.ideology: Center-left / liberal; exact economic position provisional
decisions.alignment_rationale: Explicit mission makes a positive case for liberalism. Liberalism is not automatically equivalent to a Democratic party commitment, nor does it put all writers at the same policy point.

decisions.ideology: Insufficient policy evidence; strongly Trump-critical insider commentary
decisions.alignment_rationale: The expanded reading establishes an oppositional stance toward Trump’s authoritarian behavior and a focus on insider reporting, personality and elite power. It does not provide a sufficiently broad affirmative position on redistribution, healthcare, immigration or other domains to distinguish left, center or a dissident right. Criticism of Fauci’s celebrity or Trump’s war management is not a policy platform. Keep broad ideology unclassified rather than inventing centrism.

The longer review combines explicit support for institutional reforms in the About page, an own-voice statement that Democrats should optimize their chances of winning, and a business/editorial account aligning the publication with evidence-based resistance to right-wing attacks on democracy. This supports a tentative center-left/liberal-democratic editorial placement. It is an inference about orientation, not a full policy score. Poll respondents’ preferences, projected Democratic wins and technical corrections are not themselves ideological evidence.

Additional sampled passage critiques punitive three-strikes policy and far-right claims; another defends Biden against a campaign attack. Current free-post coverage is sparse and most material is paid.

decisions.ideology: Left / progressive on Palestine and foreign policy
decisions.alignment_rationale: Explicit Palestinian-freedom mission and criticism of mainstream two-state rhetoric. It is a strong issue position, not a complete economic ideology or party identity.

decisions.publication: The Left Hook with Wajahat Ali
decisions.alignment_rationale: Condemns Biden’s Palestine policy while arguing Trump would be worse. Critical electoral support and policy disagreement must remain separate dimensions.

Compares Trump, Harris and RFK on health-care failures and corporate power; national-security reporting is highly critical of executive power. About page identifies KlipNews and a named editor, so this is no longer safely treated as a wholly solo operation.
Explicitly identifies as liberal news and commentary with roughly a dozen daily stories. Humor does not make the whole outlet fictional satire in the Borowitz sense.

Explicit anticipation of Trump’s second term and a Huck PAC donation appeal. Names a writing/editing team and Blue Diamond Media ownership; a brand byline cannot identify Mike Huckabee as every article’s actual author.
Explicit left-wing perspective; anti-war critique of Trump’s cabinet does not imply uncritical Democratic loyalty.
The seventeen access-excluded additions were not classified for the retained-cohort breakdown.

Explicit Democratic-strategist identity and advocacy for working people, protecting social insurance and confronting concentrated wealth support a liberal/center-left orientation; party loyalty is recorded separately.

decisions.ideology: Left / liberal human-rights and anti-war commentary
decisions.alignment_rationale: The reviewed writing opposes public funding of Israeli military action and defends migrants and civilians across partisan divides. Broad left/liberal placement is provisional; the review does not establish a complete economic platform.
The seventeen access-excluded additions were not classified for the retained-cohort breakdown.

Published editorial analysis affirmatively defends transgender rights and public healthcare and opposes upward wealth transfers. This is an outlet tendency; Todd Beeton’s authored pieces are not attributed to every contributor.
The seventeen access-excluded additions were not classified for the retained-cohort breakdown.

Moore explicitly advances a liberal/progressive agenda including labor rights, public provision and reproductive rights, and supports a democratic-socialist candidate against resistant Democratic leaders.

Geidner’s own analysis criticizes unequal protection of LGBTQ families and abortion restrictions. This supports a tentative socially liberal editorial placement, not a complete economic ideology or an inferred party registration.

The stated mission promotes philosophical liberalism. Reviewed contributors include a democratic socialist leaving DSA and a defender of liberal toleration critical of illiberal tactics. Their views are not Mounk’s personal policy platform; do not equate a pluralist forum with centrism.

decisions.publication: Let's Address This with Qasim Rashid
decisions.alignment_rationale: Rashid affirmatively advocates Palestinian statehood, accountability and protections for immigrants. The label concerns the stated advocacy; the article’s legal and factual claims were not independently adjudicated.

The About page explicitly names a center-to-left power-building mission. Her own article advocates replacing ICE and reducing its budget; the candidate spotlight encourages support for progressive local candidates.

decisions.publication: Letters from Leo — the American Pope & US Politics
decisions.alignment_rationale: The seventeen access-excluded additions were not classified for the retained-cohort breakdown.

Valdes-Rodriguez distinguishes socialism from authoritarianism and affirmatively favors public provision, universal healthcare and labor protections. Historical quotations by King are not treated as her own self-identification.

decisions.organization: Individual-led legal analysis with guest contributions
decisions.alignment_rationale: Litman’s own gun-law essay favors modern risk evidence, legislative judgment and agency expertise over historical analogy. A separately identified guest advocates Democratic resistance and healthcare protection; those guest arguments are not assigned to Litman personally. The broad placement remains inferential.

Her own writing calls for stronger gun laws and Democratic electoral support. A later coauthored post explicitly describes building a media ecosystem on the left and favorably treats unions and social insurance.

Two initial essays are by guest Egor Kotkin and were not assigned to the hosts. Additional host-branded episode introductions explicitly identify with the left and praise pro-labor progressive campaigns, corroborating the publication’s broad orientation.

decisions.organization: Multi-author electoral news, data and commentary service
decisions.alignment_rationale: The outlet’s own May 2024 podcast introduction calls efforts to thwart abortion rights a cynical ploy and describes the rights at stake as cherished civil rights. Its March introduction favors greater representation of progressive mothers, while the August election digest uses favorable reproductive-rights and redistricting-reform framing. Together these support a provisional liberal editorial tendency. This goes beyond predicting Democratic gains, fundraising arrangements or Daily Kos origins. Nonpartisan reporting claims are preserved as the outlet’s stated professional role; no complete economic platform or shared ideology of every byline is inferred.

The evidence supports a reporting/reform role, not a centrist policy label.

decisions.organization: Individual-led independent news and reporting operation
decisions.alignment_rationale: MacFarlane’s launch essay explains his independent reporting model and audience-guided story selection. His September editorial note reports wage and tariff developments and explicitly defends demographic diversity in newsrooms. Quoted candidates’ positions are not assigned to the reporter.

decisions.organization: Individual-led legal commentary and media-network brand
decisions.alignment_rationale: Gill explicitly supports Biden/Harris and frames a Harris victory in racial and gender-equality terms. Her framing of the transgender-service case and reproductive-rights work corroborates a tentative liberal orientation; court quotations are not her own words.

decisions.publication: The View from Rural Missouri by Jess Piper
decisions.alignment_rationale: Piper directly identifies a rural progressive point of view. Her own writing opposes public-school privatization and child-labor deregulation and favors Medicaid and reproductive rights.

Armitage expressly favors public health-insurance options and union organizing and frames policy around working-class gains and opposition to oligarchy. The review codes advocacy without certifying the numerical claims.

decisions.organization: Host-led news and commentary brand with contributors
decisions.alignment_rationale: A Don Lemon/Peter Rothpletz piece advocates universal background checks and other gun measures while defending transgender equality; Lemon’s own commentary urges Democrats to confront Trump. This supports an editorial tendency, not a claim that every guest shares it.

decisions.ideology: Broad ideology unclassified / civil liberties and clemency reform
decisions.organization: Individual-led legal analysis and rule-of-law advocacy
decisions.alignment_rationale: Oyer’s welcome essay defines a focused legal mission. Her lecture explicitly advocates equality, public defense and redemption; her pardon analysis praises relief from excessive drug sentences while defending victim restitution, accountability and principled review. These establish a civil-liberties and clemency-reform orientation, with some liberal-compatible positions, but not a sufficiently broad or distinctive left/right/centrist platform. Former career government service and anti-Trump advocacy do not decide that label.

decisions.organization: Host-led political commentary and news network
decisions.alignment_rationale: Mockler explicitly calls for strong public-health oversight and regulations and praises AOC’s opposition to corporate influence. A senator’s quoted Medicaid statements are distinguished from the author’s own regulatory argument.

Geddry favors high taxation of wealth, unions and regulated capitalism; Hurt critiques Medicare privatization. The shared About mission emphasizes environmental justice and economic inequality, supporting an outlet-level left orientation.

decisions.publication: Our Moral Moment w/ Bishop William Barber & Jonathan Wilson-Hartgrove
decisions.alignment_rationale: The authors affirm union organizing and oppose cuts to public provision paired with tax benefits for wealthy interests. Their rejection of left-versus-right branding does not make this agenda centrist; party affiliation is not inferred.
The seventeen access-excluded additions were not classified for the retained-cohort breakdown.

decisions.ideology: Center-left / socially liberal news and commentary
decisions.organization: Host-led news brand with guest reporting
decisions.alignment_rationale: A staff report affirmatively defends trans healthcare access, while Spehar critiques authoritarian or patriarchal tendencies within left influencer politics. This is a provisional socially liberal editorial tendency; a guest reporter’s prose is not assigned to Spehar personally.

decisions.publication: Free Thinking Through the Fourth Turning with Sasha Stone
decisions.alignment_rationale: Stone’s About page explicitly defends representation for the populist right while disavowing party affiliation. Her own writing supports conservative positions on abortion and gender-related policy. Independent party identity is distinct from right-leaning orientation.
Beschloss praises labor protections and union support and rejects low-tax, anti-regulation and trickle-down economic approaches in his own voice, while favoring Harris’s economic agenda.

Loury explicitly describes himself as conservative while acknowledging shifts and cross-cutting commitments. Guest Daniel Bessner’s redistributive views are not assigned to Loury. The free-expression exchange illustrates pluralism rather than an exact center position.

Williamson’s own manifesto calls for universal healthcare and economic rights and criticizes Democratic complicity in oligarchy; the labor essay affirms organizing and challenges a new Gilded Age.

decisions.alignment_rationale: The About page explicitly calls the program progressive. Pakman’s own abortion commentary favors reproductive rights and urges Democrats to use the issue to mobilize left-leaning voters.

decisions.alignment_rationale: Leonard’s full gun essay prioritizes school safety over gun access and affirms LGBTQ-inclusive education. Her own bill introduction labels the restrictions dangerous; the detailed statutory summary is not itself treated as a complete personal platform.

decisions.alignment_rationale: Kelly’s About page explicitly welcomes Trump’s victory and supports the administration’s DOJ agenda. all37_changed_decisions.publication: Hope for America with Heather Delaney Reese

alignment_method: Thirty-three public About-page openings and selected passages in two saved public posts per retained publication; additional full-text readings logged for ambiguous cases. The six-publication close review adds source-linked saved-post evidence for four additions and two original publications. Selection is purposive, not a representative article sample. Full-versus-passage scopes are listed per source.
limits: This is a content-access selection rule, not proof of complete articles, complete historical archives or complete discussions.
Keeping a publication does not mean its restricted posts have become readable; some restricted months and short previews remain.
Politics and business model can correlate with content access; this cohort is not representative of all political writers.
Previously reported pilots and the working manuscript used other frames and have not been re-estimated on this cohort.
The completed planned collection pass is a finite public-discussion sample, not all comments on all articles.
Three retained reporting/legal publications remain unclassified on broad ideology; nonpartisan work is not automatically centrist.

The six-publication close review resolves Kinzinger and Wilson as center-right/conservative and The Downballot as a tentative liberal editorial tendency, using saved posts rather than biography alone.

retained_empty_month_audit.definition: Zero saved post records between first and last observed post months; not restricted-body posts.
retained_empty_month_audit.scope: All four retained publications with interior empty months, using existing saved raw archive responses and read-only databases. No new network requests.
retained_empty_month_audit.interpretation: These gaps are already absent from returned saved archive pages, rather than posts lost during database ingestion. This does not distinguish a publishing break, removed/migrated content, or omissions in Substack archive responses, and does not prove the source archive complete.
